chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about feeding ten poor people or feeding sixty poor people: is that combined for one person to whom it is given? He said: No, but a person gives to one person as Allah, the Exalted, said. I said: So should the man give it to his relatives if they are needy? He said: Yes. I said: So should he give it to the weak from those outside the Wilayah? He said: Yes, and those of the Wilayah are more beloved to me. So it does not contradict the first report, because repetition is permissible only when the person does not find the number of men upon whom feeding is obligatory; then it is permissible for him to repeat it upon them. But if he finds them, it is appropriate that he gives to each one of them until he completes the number.

key_terms.التَّكْرِيرُ: Repetition (giving to the same person multiple times)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to give the full amount of charity or khums to one poor person, or should it be distributed among many?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a general principle of diversity in distribution for expiation (kaffarah) or charity, preferring to spread benefits among distinct individuals rather than concentrating them on one, unless the pool of eligible recipients is insufficient to meet the required count. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on maximizing social welfare and ensuring equitable resource allocation, while still allowing flexibility for kinship ties (Qarabah) and those within the Wilayah.
